note: REVISED after user rejected the first selection as boring: 'не виглядає байтово і цікаво'. Three of the original six (tariff revenue $2bn/day, gas $1.98/gallon, China 'trillion dollars') were dry numeric fact-check gaffes with no visual punch -- 'he said a wrong number' does not work on screen. The Krebs executive-order signing was dropped for the same reason (a man signing a paper and repeating a claim, no reactive moment). Kept the two stories with real visual/reactive punch (Abrego Garcia tattoo clash, two dolls) and replaced the rest with four stories that have an actual visual gag, reaction shot, or on-camera absurdity: the two previously-discarded-but-viable backups (pope joke, Liberation Day tariff-board reveal) plus two new finds from additional research (Easter Egg Roll autopen rant to confused kids, YMCA dance at the Michigan 100-days rally). Every entry checked for real YouTube/news-channel footage before being considered usable (format.md requires real SOT, no text-only claims).

candidates.claim: Trump insists a digitally altered Truth Social photo proves Kilmar Abrego Garcia has 'MS-13' tattooed on his knuckles, clashing on-camera with ABC's Terry Moran when shown the real photo.
candidates.video_status: confirmed - ABC News aired the full Oval Office interview (Apr 29) where Trump and Terry Moran argue over the photo; widely re-clipped by ABC News, Rolling Stone-linked footage, and Forbes; also C-SPAN pool coverage of the Truth Social image reveal.
candidates.rank_signal: pants-fire (PolitiFact, Apr 29 statement); kept -- user confirmed this is visual, absurd, reactive, already a famous moment

candidates.claim: In a televised Cabinet meeting, Trump dismisses tariff/trade-war concerns by saying kids might 'have two dolls instead of 30 dolls... and maybe the two dolls will cost a couple of bucks more.'
candidates.video_status: confirmed - WSJ News YouTube upload 'Trump: Maybe the Children Will Have Two Dolls Instead of 30 Dolls', plus Washington Post video and wide cable replay (MSNBC 'Donny Two Dolls').
candidates.rank_signal: widely covered gaffe; kept -- user confirmed this is visual, absurd, reactive, already a famous moment

candidates.claim: Trump closes his 100-days rally in Warren, Michigan by breaking into his signature 'Trump dance' -- arm pumps and shoulder shimmy -- to the Village People's 'YMCA' in front of a roaring crowd.
candidates.video_status: confirmed - C-SPAN 'User Clip: Trump Dances to YMCA' from the Apr 29, 2025 rally; separate YouTube upload 'Donald Trump dances to end Michigan rally celebrating 100 days in office'; clipped and shared widely including by the Trump War Room account.
candidates.rank_signal: no PolitiFact rating (not a factual claim) -- included on pure visual/reactive merit per revised brief: absurd, physically comedic, huge crowd reaction, works with sound off

candidates.claim: At the White House Easter Egg Roll, while coloring eggs with small children, Trump veers into a rant claiming Biden 'had an autopen follow him' because he was 'incapable of signing things' -- one child audibly responds 'What?'
candidates.video_status: confirmed - White House pool video of the South Lawn event (Apr 21, 2025), re-clipped by multiple outlets specifically for the autopen tangent and the children's confused reactions.
candidates.rank_signal: no PolitiFact rating (a fabricated anecdote, not a numeric claim) -- included on visual/reactive merit: a sitting president randomly lecturing bewildered small children is inherently absurd and has a clean reaction shot

candidates.claim: Trump unveils a poster-board of 'reciprocal tariffs' by country in the Rose Garden, calling it 'Liberation Day' and 'our declaration of economic independence' -- the board's math was later shown to be a flat formula, not real reciprocal calculations.
candidates.video_status: confirmed - the full Rose Garden event was carried live by every major network and is on C-SPAN/YouTube; the poster-board reveal is a distinct, widely re-clipped visual beat within it.
candidates.rank_signal: previously held back for crowding out fact-check density, but re-evaluated: a giant novelty poster board of made-up tariff math held up on an easel in the Rose Garden is exactly the visual gag the format needs

candidates.claim: Boarding Marine One for his 100-days rally, Trump tells reporters 'I'd like to be pope... that would be my number one choice,' days after Pope Francis's death.
candidates.video_status: confirmed - multiple YouTube uploads of the exact tarmac exchange (BBC News, and several US outlets), viral clip.
candidates.rank_signal: previously held back to avoid crowding fact-check density stories; re-evaluated as the weakest but still usable of the six -- real tarmac footage, absurd out-of-context quote, sets up the AI pope image that followed days later

candidates.claim: Signing an executive order to strip Chris Krebs's security clearance and order a DOJ probe, Trump repeats that the 2020 election was 'badly rigged' and calls Krebs a 'wise guy.'
candidates.video_status: confirmed - C-SPAN clip of the signing remarks exists.
candidates.rank_signal: cut in revision -- consequential policy story, but visually it is just a man signing a paper and repeating a claim; no reaction shot, no absurd visual, doesn't clear the new visual/reactive bar

candidates.claim: At an executive order signing and an NRCC speech, Trump claims the US is 'taking in almost $2 billion a day' from his new tariffs -- actual Treasury daily customs revenue that day was about $192 million.
candidates.video_status: confirmed but unused for its visual weakness, not sourcing.
candidates.rank_signal: cut in revision -- a dry numeric fact-check gaffe, 'he said a wrong number,' with no visual punch

candidates.claim: Trump tells reporters at the White House 'we had a couple of states where gasoline was at $1.98 a gallon' -- no state's average was even close; lowest was ~$2.70 (Mississippi/Tennessee).
candidates.video_status: confirmed but unused for its visual weakness, not sourcing.
candidates.rank_signal: cut in revision -- a dry numeric fact-check gaffe, 'he said a wrong number,' with no visual punch

candidates.claim: At an event and again at the April 10 Cabinet meeting, Trump repeats 'China made $1 trillion off trade with the United States' -- the real 2024 US-China goods deficit was about $295 billion.
candidates.video_status: confirmed but unused for its visual weakness, not sourcing.
candidates.rank_signal: cut in revision -- a dry numeric fact-check gaffe, 'he said a wrong number,' with no visual punch

candidates.claim: Trump posts an AI-generated image of himself dressed as the pope; JD Vance defends it.
candidates.video_status: discarded - the 'moment' is a static AI-generated image on Truth Social, not real footage of an event; violates the real-footage-only rule even though it's arguably April-adjacent, and the date actually falls in May.

candidates.claim: Trump tells Time Magazine he's made '200 deals' on tariffs and negotiations will be 'finished' in 3-4 weeks.
candidates.video_status: weak - this was a print/phone interview with Time, no camera crew; only stills exist, no usable SOT video of the actual quote.

candidates.claim: Reports emerge that Defense Secretary Hegseth shared Yemen strike details in a second, personal Signal chat with his wife and brother.
candidates.video_status: weak for this angle - the news itself is about a private chat app, no camera footage of the moment.

candidates.claim: Over 1,000 international students had visas revoked/status terminated, several for minor infractions like speeding tickets, before the administration abruptly reversed course April 25.
candidates.video_status: weak - a policy/legal story without one clean absurd SOT moment from Trump himself.

candidates.claim: Trump posts a Blues-Brothers-style 'mission from God' meme about tariffs on Truth Social.
candidates.video_status: weak - a static meme image posted online, not a filmed moment; no real SOT to cut to.

candidates.claim: At his Michigan 100-days rally, Trump laughs off a protester, joking 'I thought it was a guy.'
candidates.video_status: plausible - rally is televised, but only one weak source found and the joke reads as a mean-spirited jab at a woman's appearance rather than an absurd factual claim; lower priority.
candidates.verdict: not selected - kept as backup, thin sourcing

candidates.claim: A reporter's boom microphone knocks into Trump's face at a Joint Base Andrews press gaggle; Trump deadpans 'she just became a big story tonight.'
candidates.video_status: confirmed - widely clipped by Fox News, TMZ and others; genuinely visual and funny.
candidates.verdict: DISCARD - wrong month, this happened March 14, 2025, not April
